instructions: Dust a large sheet of parchment generously with some of the cornstarch. Roll the red bean paste into 12 balls, about 1 tablespoon each, and set them on a plate.
In a microwave safe bowl, whisk the mochiko and sugar. Add 3/4 cup of water and whisk until smooth.
Cover the bowl loosely and microwave on high for 2 minutes. Stir with a wet spatula, cover and microwave for 30 seconds, until the dough turns slightly clear.

Transfer the dough to the parchment and dust the top with more cornstarch. Roll it to about 1/8 inch thick and cut out 12 circles with a 3 1/2 inch cutter or a glass. Gather the scraps and roll them again for any missing circles.
Set a ball of red bean paste on each circle. Gather the edges up around it and pinch them closed.
Dust the seams with cornstarch and set each daifuku seam side down. Brush off the extra cornstarch before eating.
Serve the same day. Keep leftovers in a closed container in the fridge for up to 2 days.
method_notes: The lead and other versions agree on a wrapper of mochiko, sugar and water, cooked in the microwave and dusted with cornstarch. The lead makes the red bean paste from dried beans, which takes about 90 minutes; store-bought sweet red bean paste is used here so the snack stays short. Only mochiko, sugar, cornstarch and red bean paste are in it, so it stays gluten-free; check the paste label.
